name: Las Vegas
summary: A desert metro in the Mojave built around the casino resorts of the Strip, with a 24-hour hospitality economy, sprawling master-planned suburbs and red-rock country on its edges.

curated-2026-10.title: Las Vegas places and neighbourhoods written for Prospero Companion
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighbourhood centres.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for Las Vegas (Harry Reid International Airport)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals; refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available. Summer heat is extreme (often above 110F in July) and most summer rain falls in brief monsoon storms from July to September.

neighborhoods.name: The Strip (Paradise)
neighborhoods.summary: Las Vegas Boulevard's megaresorts, casinos, arenas and high-rise condo towers in unincorporated Paradise, busy around the clock.

neighborhoods.name: Convention Center and Paradise Road
neighborhoods.summary: The blocks east of the Strip around the Las Vegas Convention Center, with older condos, apartments and off-Strip hotels.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown and Fremont Street
neighborhoods.summary: The original casino district under the Fremont Street canopy, plus Fremont East bars, city and county offices, and Symphony Park.

neighborhoods.name: Arts District (18b)
neighborhoods.summary: Former industrial blocks south of downtown turned galleries, antique shops, craft bars and restaurants, with new apartment buildings.

neighborhoods.name: Chinatown (Spring Mountain Road)
neighborhoods.summary: Miles of strip-mall restaurants along Spring Mountain Road west of the Strip, many open late for casino workers and chefs.

neighborhoods.name: Medical District
neighborhoods.summary: The hospital cluster around University Medical Center near Charleston Boulevard and US 95, with older ranch homes and apartments.

neighborhoods.name: University District
neighborhoods.summary: The area around UNLV on Maryland Parkway, with student apartments, cheap eats and midcentury houses.

neighborhoods.name: East Las Vegas
neighborhoods.summary: Working-class east valley of ranch homes and apartments, with a large Latino community and taquerias along Fremont and Charleston.

neighborhoods.name: North Las Vegas
neighborhoods.summary: A separate city of newer subdivisions, warehouses and older neighbourhoods, next to Nellis Air Force Base.

neighborhoods.name: Centennial Hills
neighborhoods.summary: Northwest suburbs of stucco subdivisions and shopping centres on the road toward Mount Charleston.

neighborhoods.name: Summerlin
neighborhoods.summary: A large master-planned community on the west edge of the valley with trails, parks, a ballpark and Downtown Summerlin, beside Red Rock Canyon.

neighborhoods.name: Spring Valley
neighborhoods.summary: Central-west suburbs of apartment complexes and tract homes, where Chinatown's restaurants spill west along Spring Mountain and Rainbow.

neighborhoods.name: Southwest (Enterprise)
neighborhoods.summary: The fast-growing southwest valley of master-planned subdivisions like Mountain's Edge, plus data centres and warehouses.

neighborhoods.name: Southern Highlands
neighborhoods.summary: A master-planned community at the south end of the valley built around a private golf club, with gated enclaves.

neighborhoods.name: Green Valley (Henderson)
neighborhoods.summary: Henderson's older master-planned core of parks, schools and shopping centres, popular with families.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Henderson
neighborhoods.summary: Henderson's original town centre around Water Street, with newer subdivisions climbing toward the River Mountains.

neighborhoods.name: Lake Las Vegas
neighborhoods.summary: A resort community around a man-made lake at the eastern edge of Henderson, with Mediterranean-style condos and a village of restaurants.

neighborhoods.name: Boulder City
neighborhoods.summary: A small, quiet town built for the Hoover Dam workers, with no casinos and Lake Mead on its doorstep.

transit.name: RTC Transit buses
transit.summary: The Regional Transportation Commission's valley-wide bus network, running 24 hours on major routes.

transit.name: The Deuce
transit.summary: Double-decker RTC buses running around the clock along the Strip to downtown.

transit.name: Las Vegas Monorail
transit.summary: Elevated line behind the east side of the Strip from MGM Grand to SAHARA, with a stop at the Convention Center.

transit.name: Driving
transit.summary: How most residents get around: wide arterials, the I-15 and the 215 beltway, and plentiful parking off the Strip.

transit.name: Rideshare and taxis
transit.summary: Uber, Lyft and cabs with dedicated pickup areas at every resort and the airport.

transit.name: Walking
transit.summary: Practical on the Strip and downtown via pedestrian bridges, though distances between resorts are long and summer heat is punishing.

places.name: Fountains of Bellagio
places.summary: Free water shows set to music on the lake in front of Bellagio, every half hour or so from the afternoon.

places.name: Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Gardens
places.summary: Free indoor garden with elaborate floral displays that change with the seasons.

places.name: "O" by Cirque du Soleil
places.summary: Long-running water-themed Cirque show staged in and above a pool at Bellagio.

places.name: Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign
places.summary: The 1959 neon sign on the south Strip, with a small parking lot and a queue for photos.

places.name: High Roller
places.summary: Giant observation wheel at The LINQ with glass cabins and Strip views; a full turn takes about half an hour.

places.name: The LINQ Promenade
places.summary: Open-air street of bars, restaurants and shops between the Strip and the High Roller.

places.name: Brooklyn Bowl
places.summary: Bowling alley and concert venue on the LINQ Promenade.

places.name: Grand Canal Shoppes gondolas
places.summary: Gondola rides along indoor canals under a painted sky at The Venetian, with an outdoor canal on the Strip.

places.name: Sphere
places.summary: The LED-covered globe behind The Venetian, showing immersive films and concert residencies on a wraparound screen.

places.name: The Forum Shops at Caesars
places.summary: Luxury mall at Caesars Palace built like a Roman street, with a spiral escalator and animatronic fountain shows.

places.name: Bacchanal Buffet
places.summary: Caesars Palace's huge buffet with hundreds of dishes across live-cooking stations.

places.name: Fashion Show Las Vegas
places.summary: Big indoor mall on the Strip with department stores and a runway in the centre court.

places.name: Tacos El Gordo
places.summary: Tijuana-style taqueria on the north Strip with adobada shaved off the spit, open into the small hours.

places.name: Peppermill Restaurant & Fireside Lounge
places.summary: Twenty-four-hour diner and neon-lit lounge with a firepit, unchanged since the 1970s.

places.name: Hash House A Go Go at The LINQ
places.summary: Brunch spot known for enormous portions of farm-style breakfast.

places.name: Golden Steer Steakhouse
places.summary: Old-Vegas steakhouse from 1958 with red leather booths and tableside Caesar salad.

places.name: T-Mobile Arena
places.summary: Home of the Vegas Golden Knights, also used for big concerts and fights.

places.name: Allegiant Stadium
places.summary: Domed home of the Las Vegas Raiders and UNLV football, just west of I-15 from Mandalay Bay.

places.name: Shark Reef Aquarium
places.summary: Aquarium at Mandalay Bay with a walk-through shark tunnel.

places.name: The STRAT SkyPod
places.summary: Observation deck atop the STRAT tower at the north end of the Strip, with thrill rides on the roof.

places.name: AREA15 and Omega Mart
places.summary: Immersive art and entertainment complex just west of the Strip, anchored by Meow Wolf's Omega Mart.

places.name: Pinball Hall of Fame
places.summary: Warehouse of playable vintage pinball and arcade machines near the Welcome sign.

places.name: Fremont Street Experience
places.summary: Pedestrian mall of old casinos under a huge LED canopy with nightly light shows, buskers and a zipline.

places.name: The Mob Museum
places.summary: National museum of organised crime and law enforcement in the former federal courthouse, with a speakeasy and distillery downstairs.

places.name: The Neon Museum
places.summary: Outdoor "Neon Boneyard" of rescued casino signs, best on the evening guided tours when some are relit.

places.name: Downtown Container Park
places.summary: Small boutiques and bars in stacked shipping containers behind a fire-breathing praying mantis sculpture.

places.name: Atomic Liquors
places.summary: Fremont East bar that dates to the 1950s, billed as the oldest freestanding bar in the city.

places.name: Stadium Swim at Circa
places.summary: Tiered pool amphitheatre at Circa resort facing a giant screen showing live sports.

places.name: The Smith Center for the Performing Arts
places.summary: Art deco performing arts centre in Symphony Park hosting touring Broadway, the symphony and the ballet.

places.name: Discovery Children's Museum
places.summary: Three floors of hands-on exhibits in Symphony Park.

places.name: PublicUs
places.summary: Airy Fremont East coffee shop and bakery popular for laptop mornings.

places.name: Esther's Kitchen
places.summary: Arts District Italian restaurant known for house-made pasta and sourdough.

places.name: Velveteen Rabbit
places.summary: Moody craft cocktail bar with a patio in the Arts District.

places.name: Arts Factory
places.summary: Converted building of galleries and studios at the heart of 18b and its First Friday art walk.

places.name: Pho Kim Long
places.summary: Vietnamese noodle house on Spring Mountain Road open around the clock.

places.name: Raku
places.summary: Small Japanese robata grill famous for house-made tofu, open late and popular with off-duty chefs.

places.name: Chinatown Plaza
places.summary: The original 1990s Chinatown mall on Spring Mountain Road, with a gate, Asian grocers and restaurants.

places.name: Herbs & Rye
places.summary: Dim, award-winning cocktail bar on West Sahara with half-price steaks at happy hour.

places.name: Lotus of Siam
places.summary: Celebrated Thai restaurant known for Northern Thai dishes and a long riesling list.

places.name: Ellis Island Casino & Brewery
places.summary: Locals' casino off the Strip with a brewery, karaoke lounge and a cheap steak special.

places.name: Thomas & Mack Center
places.summary: UNLV's arena for Runnin' Rebels basketball and the National Finals Rodeo.

places.name: Marjorie Barrick Museum of Art
places.summary: Free contemporary art museum on the UNLV campus.

places.name: Springs Preserve
places.summary: Desert gardens, trails and museums at the site of the springs where Las Vegas began.

places.name: Las Vegas North Premium Outlets
places.summary: Large open-air outlet mall just west of downtown.

places.name: Freed's Bakery
places.summary: Family bakery since the 1950s, known for elaborate custom cakes.

places.name: Clark County Wetlands Park
places.summary: Ponds, cottonwoods and trails along the Las Vegas Wash with a nature centre and good birdwatching.

places.name: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area
places.summary: Red sandstone cliffs on a 13-mile scenic loop drive with hiking and climbing, minutes from Summerlin.

places.name: Las Vegas Ballpark
places.summary: Minor-league home of the Las Vegas Aviators, with a pool beyond the outfield.

places.name: Downtown Summerlin
places.summary: Open-air shopping and dining district at the centre of Summerlin.

places.name: Downtown Summerlin Farmers Market
places.summary: Weekly farmers market with produce, baked goods and food stalls.

places.name: Floyd Lamb Park at Tule Springs
places.summary: Shady historic ranch park with ponds, peacocks and old cottonwoods.

places.name: Mount Charleston
places.summary: Pine forest trails in the Spring Mountains, about 45 minutes from the northwest valley and markedly cooler, with winter snow.

places.name: Craig Ranch Regional Park
places.summary: Large park in North Las Vegas with a skate park, dog parks and an outdoor amphitheatre.

places.name: Valley of Fire State Park
places.summary: Red sandstone formations and petroglyphs about an hour northeast of the city.

places.name: Ethel M Chocolates factory and cactus garden
places.summary: Chocolate factory with a free botanical cactus garden that is lit up for the holidays.

places.name: The District at Green Valley Ranch
places.summary: Walkable shopping street beside the Green Valley Ranch resort.

places.name: Water Street District
places.summary: Henderson's small historic main street with an events plaza, restaurants and a weekly farmers market.

places.name: Sloan Canyon National Conservation Area
places.summary: Desert hiking south of Henderson to a canyon of ancient petroglyphs.

places.name: River Mountains Loop Trail
places.summary: Paved 34-mile loop linking Henderson, Boulder City and Lake Mead.

places.name: MonteLago Village
places.summary: Lakeside village of restaurants, paddleboard and boat rentals at Lake Las Vegas.

places.name: Hoover Dam
places.summary: The 1930s concrete dam on the Colorado River at the Arizona line, with tours and a bypass bridge walkway.

places.name: Lake Mead National Recreation Area
places.summary: Reservoir behind the dam for boating, kayaking and swimming at Boulder Beach, with the bathtub ring of drought visible.

places.name: Historic Railroad Trail
places.summary: Flat gravel trail through five railroad tunnels above Lake Mead toward Hoover Dam; bighorn sheep are often seen.

places.name: Seven Magic Mountains
places.summary: Ugo Rondinone's stacks of day-glo painted boulders in the desert off I-15, about 20 minutes south of the valley.

colleges.name: Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV
William S. Boyd School of Law
College of Southern Nevada (North Las Vegas campus)

employers.name: MGM Resorts International
employers.summary: Runs Bellagio, MGM Grand, Aria, Mandalay Bay and other Strip resorts; the largest private employer in the state.

employers.name: Caesars Entertainment
employers.summary: Operates Caesars Palace, The LINQ, Paris, Harrah's and other Strip resorts.

employers.name: Wynn Las Vegas and Encore
employers.summary: Luxury resort pair on the north Strip with high-end shops and nightlife.

employers.name: The Venetian Resort
employers.summary: All-suite resort with a casino, shopping canals and a large expo hall.

employers.name: Resorts World Las Vegas
employers.summary: Newer north Strip resort with a casino, three Hilton hotels and a food hall.

employers.name: Station Casinos (Red Rock Resorts)
employers.summary: Locals' casino company headquartered in Summerlin, running Red Rock, Green Valley Ranch, Durango and others.

employers.name: Cirque du Soleil resident shows
employers.summary: Several permanent Cirque productions in Strip resort theatres, with artists, musicians and technical crews.

employers.name: Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority
employers.summary: Runs the Las Vegas Convention Center and markets the city to visitors and trade shows.

employers.name: Harry Reid International Airport
employers.summary: The county-run airport just east of the south Strip, with airline, cargo, concession and security jobs.

employers.name: Allegiant Air
employers.summary: Low-cost airline headquartered in Summerlin.

employers.name: Switch
employers.summary: Data centre company with large campuses in the southwest valley.

employers.name: Zappos
employers.summary: Online shoe and clothing retailer headquartered in the old City Hall downtown.

employers.name: Las Vegas Raiders
employers.summary: NFL team with its headquarters and practice facility in Henderson.

employers.name: University Medical Center of Southern Nevada
employers.summary: The county public hospital with the state's only Level I trauma centre, and UNLV's main teaching hospital.

employers.name: Sunrise Hospital and Medical Center
employers.summary: Large HCA hospital on Maryland Parkway with a children's hospital.

employers.name: Dignity Health St. Rose Dominican
employers.summary: Catholic hospital group with several campuses in Henderson.

employers.name: Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health
employers.summary: Neurology clinic and research centre in a Frank Gehry building in Symphony Park.

employers.name: UNLV
employers.summary: Faculty, research and staff jobs at the main university campus.

employers.name: Clark County School District
employers.summary: One of the largest school districts in the country, chronically short of teachers.

employers.name: Clark County government and courts
employers.summary: County agencies at the Government Center and the Regional Justice Center downtown; the county also governs the Strip.

employers.name: City of Las Vegas
employers.summary: City Hall and municipal departments on Main Street.

employers.name: Nellis Air Force Base
employers.summary: Major Air Force base for advanced fighter training, with civilian and contractor engineering jobs.

employers.name: Las Vegas Review-Journal
employers.summary: The state's largest daily newspaper.

career_hubs.name: The Strip resorts
career_hubs.summary: Tens of thousands of casino, hotel, kitchen, spa, pool and show jobs running 24 hours a day.

career_hubs.name: Convention Center and Paradise Road
career_hubs.summary: Trade-show work around the Las Vegas Convention Center and resort expo halls.

career_hubs.name: Downtown and the Arts District
career_hubs.summary: City and county offices, the courts, Fremont Street casinos, tech offices and small creative studios.

career_hubs.name: Medical District and UNLV
career_hubs.summary: UMC, the UNLV medical school and nearby hospitals, plus the main university campus.

career_hubs.name: Summerlin offices
career_hubs.summary: Corporate headquarters, banks and real-estate offices in the west valley.

career_hubs.name: Henderson
career_hubs.summary: Hospitals, health sciences schools, the Raiders' headquarters and fast-growing suburban retail.

career_hubs.name: Southwest warehouses and data centres
career_hubs.summary: Distribution centres, data centres and home building in the growing southwest valley.

career_hubs.name: Nellis and North Las Vegas
career_hubs.summary: The air base, industrial parks and warehouses along I-15 north.

climate.summary: Hot desert: very hot, dry summers with brief monsoon storms, mild sunny winters with cold nights, and very little rain at any time of year.

months.note: Coolest month; sunny days, chilly nights.
Mild and dry; occasional windy storms.
Warm and dry; prime hiking season ends.
Hottest month; 110F days and monsoon storms.
Extreme heat; monsoon flash floods possible.

annual_events.name: CES
annual_events.summary: The giant consumer electronics trade show fills the Convention Center and hotels in early January.

annual_events.name: Chinese New Year in Chinatown
annual_events.summary: Lion dances and celebrations on Spring Mountain Road, with decorations at Strip resorts.

annual_events.name: First Friday
annual_events.summary: Monthly evening art walk with open galleries, food trucks and live music.

annual_events.name: NASCAR at Las Vegas Motor Speedway
annual_events.summary: Cup Series race weekends in spring and autumn at the speedway in the northeast valley.

annual_events.name: Aviators baseball season
annual_events.summary: Triple-A baseball nights at Las Vegas Ballpark.

annual_events.name: Electric Daisy Carnival
annual_events.summary: Huge three-night electronic music festival at Las Vegas Motor Speedway.

annual_events.name: Punk Rock Bowling
annual_events.summary: Memorial Day weekend punk festival downtown with a bowling tournament.

annual_events.name: Raiders football season
annual_events.summary: NFL game days at Allegiant Stadium.

annual_events.name: Golden Knights hockey season
annual_events.summary: NHL games with elaborate pregame shows at T-Mobile Arena.

annual_events.name: SEMA Show
annual_events.summary: Car customisation trade show that brings custom builds to the Convention Center.

annual_events.name: Las Vegas Grand Prix
annual_events.summary: Formula 1 night race on a street circuit along the Strip, with weeks of road closures.

annual_events.name: National Finals Rodeo
annual_events.summary: Ten nights of championship rodeo at the Thomas & Mack Center, with cowboy events across town.

annual_events.name: New Year's Eve on the Strip
annual_events.summary: The Strip closes to cars for crowds and rooftop fireworks at midnight.
